theorem: On a retained cyclic sheet and a separate two-real-coordinate plane, coherently route T of a fixed generator on one arm and the rational R=(aI+bJ)/c on the other. Apply H to the arm before and after, accepting its plus output. The complete port pair is (T⊗I±I⊗R)/2. The commuting operators share joint sectors (k,s); T acts by exp(2πik/q), J by s i. Born conditioning multiplies their weights by p_ks=(1+cos(2πk/q−sφ))/2. The localized real launch gives weight 1/(2q) per sector. For |φ−2π/q|<π/q the maximizers are the two correlated pairs k=s mod q. Put G=cos²(delta/2), B=cos²((2π/q−delta)/2) for delta=absolute angle error. After r retained plus records wrong/correct odds ≤(q−1)(B/G)^r, correct joint mass G^r/q. Choosing angle error O(1/r) makes correct mass approach 1/q at this fixed order. At fixed nonzero angle mismatch G<1, insisting on indefinitely many bright records kills yield. For arbitrary input replace 1/q by its prior on the correlated subspace; zero initial overlap cannot be created. A single fresh localized read always has probability 1/2 and resetting every record gives 2^-r. A complete ordinary folded sheet preparation uncorrelated with the rebit initially has only half its weight in the wanted chiral relation.
readout: After accepting, compare a held power T^d with I on the reference arm to obtain cosine contrast, or with the real signed quarter-turn J for sine contrast. Both survive global conjugation since s changes with k. Both can be negative; neither is an absolute choice of complex square root of -1. Two sheets calibrated on the SAME plane align their chiral signs and powers of their product yield cosine and sine on the joint cyclotomic order. Independent uncorrelated planes would not align those signs. Conditioned wrong mass η perturbs any contrast by at most 2η. The operational field generated by these limiting contrasts is the real field Q(cos(2π/q),sin(2π/q)), the maximal real subfield of Q(zeta_lcm(q,4)); it does not give arbitrary complex numbers as probabilities. Repeated coherent synthesis and additional fields can extend the available apparatus.
gate: For Pythagorean a²+b²=c², pad K=2^ceil(log2(|a|+|b|)). Reuse the native Walsh-signed SELECT structure. Acted block: |a| labels implement sign(a)I, |b| labels sign(b)J; idle block: c labels implement I; all other labels flip the blank validity bit reversibly. Two full-index Walsh layers and one common projector onto flag-zero/index-zero realize success Kraus (c/K)(R direct-sum I). Full complement is retained as one outcome, never reading a distinguishing data/name flag. All code input states have the same pass probability p=c²/K²>1/8. For retry use the actual inverse W†, with J†=−J; this SELECT need not be an involution. Alternating W†/W and coarse anchor reads on a failed attempt gives residual (1−p)(1−2p(1−p))^N, expected 1+1/p calls when 0<p<1. The sheet shift is separately applied only after a successful rotation port, while the coherent comparison arms remain unread. Gate retries and timeout are separate from subsequent plus/minus read. The two arms need matched phase, timing and discarded-route information.
finite_apparatus: Stereographic slope rounding with denominator m and an exact signed quarter-turn gives rational orthogonals within 1/m chord distance, including clocked idle blocks. A known finite circuit of L such plane rotations and signed permutations, with ordinary common projectors, changes its unconditional instrument probabilities by at most L/m in total variation by telescoping contractive unitaries and retaining an outcome register. General finite complex unitaries can be realified and decomposed into finitely many real plane rotations and signed permutations; synthesis needs addressable two-coordinate pairs and spectator matching. Finite rational programs give exact rational laws on rational localized real input, even when the named target limit has algebraic records. Conditional probabilities also need the original herald mass bounded away from zero. Compilation alone does not establish the probability law or choose an absolute field embedding.
grounding: The fundamental angular target can be constructed as the smallest positive order-q turn relative to a chosen oriented circle. A physical synthesizer needs held addressable I,J and the fixed sheet stroke plus coherent controlled use. For the examples an additional finite program search uses only integer operations: enumerate rational rotations in the first quadrant, count crossings of the positive real ray under q powers, and require the nearest unwrapped return to have winding one. A final point with positive real part bounds angular error by 2*abs(Im(R^q))/q. Refining the grid yields arbitrary accuracy by density and the simple oriented order-q root. A finite grid and integer test need no numerical sine/cosine input. The quarter orientation and order are operational assumptions. Other instruments still require matched controls or a calibrated operationally equivalent apparatus. Only the relative sheet/reference chirality is measured. Complementing the real plane or simultaneously relabeling the entire sheet apparatus leaves the experiment invariant. Without the held comparison arm, native powers give ordered folded cosines; they do not themselves supply this synchronized reference or its heralded state preparation.
